newsitem.title: USA: Phillips, Daewoo, others in gas plant venture.
newsitem.headline: Phillips, Daewoo, others in gas plant venture.

text.p: An international consortium will build a $1 billion liquefied natural gas (LNG) plant in British Columbia that will be the largest LNG facility in North America, Phillips Petroleum Co. said Wednesday.
The gas, produced in Canada, would be exported from the western Canadian plant to South Korea's Korea Gas, Phillips said in a statement.

Phillips Petroleum Canada Ltd. holds a 35 percent interest in the project, while South Korean industrial conglomerate Daewoo Corp. has 25 percent, PAC-RIM LNG Inc. of Calgary, Alberta, 20 percent and San Francisco-based construction and engineering giant Bechtel Group Inc.'s Bechtel Enterprises 10 percent.

Korea Gas is expected to pick up the remaining 10 percent stake, Bartlesville, Okla.-based Phillips said. One or more Canadian producers is expected to join the consortium as the project moves forward.
Under a memorandum of participation, consortium members will build the plant near Kitimat, British Columbia, that will produce 3.5 million metric tons of LNG a year.
Construction is expected to begin later this year, with the first deliveries to South Korea targeted for late 1999, Phillips said.
A final agreement remains to be negotiated. The plant also requires approval from the government and the companies' boards.
Phillips has operated an LNG plant on Alaska's Kenai Peninsula since 1969. The plant exports 1.3 million metric tons per year to Japan.
Phillips had profits of $1.3 billion on revenues of $15.8 billion last year. Its stock dipped 75 cents to $39.50 in consolidated early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
